scenes.title: Pudding Lane
scenes.text: A little after midnight on Sunday the second of September, sixteen sixty-six, a fire broke out in a baker's shop on Pudding Lane.

scenes.title: Sunday to Wednesday
scenes.text: It burned until Wednesday. Only when the wind dropped and firebreaks took hold was the fire finally over.

scenes.title: The loss
scenes.text: By then, an estimated thirteen thousand houses, about eighty-seven parish churches, and Saint Paul's Cathedral had been destroyed.

scenes.title: How many died?
scenes.text: The death toll is still debated. The traditional figure is just six, but some historians think it was far higher.

scenes.title: Brick and stone
scenes.text: London was rebuilt in brick and stone, not wood. Christopher Wren rebuilt Saint Paul's, and the Monument, two hundred and two feet tall, still marks the fire.
